I will plant the crop system I know best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. This is the normal pattern on the North China Plain, it fits our climate, and it matches how rain falls here. Summer gets most of the rain, so maize is easier to carry with less irrigation. Wheat grows through the dry part of the year, so I will keep wheat too, but I will control water and fertilizer instead of pushing for the very highest yield. I will not switch a big area into cotton, peanuts, or vegetables because that would raise my risk in sales, labor, and management. I would rather make a steady grain plan I understand well and can manage on time.

If I were making the decisions myself this year, I would use improved seed, not old saved seed and not expensive complicated seed on every crop. I would keep the whole farm in one wheat-maize rotation so field work is simple. After maize harvest, I would prepare the land for wheat with rotary tillage and return straw where possible. For wheat, I would give more fertilizer and about three irrigations because that crop is the one that needs help here. I would watch weeds early, then rust, aphids, and later disease pressure, so about two pesticide passes in a normal year. After wheat harvest, I would sow summer maize quickly, keep residue on the field, and use no-tillage or minimum disturbance to save moisture and time. Maize usually catches the summer rain, so I would plan only one irrigation, or skip it if rainfall is good. I would keep pest sprays limited unless pressure is real. My goal is stable yield, lower water use, and fewer unnecessary costs.
